commit_scope: Keep app.hati.earth Sheet balance reads inside the same-origin proxy budget by moving blocking grocery graph reads off the async event loop and bounding the complete totals handler.

task_card.goal: Stop slow authenticated grocery totals reads from outliving the Hati proxy and amplifying into overlapping Sheet requests.
done_when: Grocery board graph reads cannot block the async event loop.

The totals wall clock starts before membership and graph reads; database, membership, balance, and reconciliation policy operations own the same absolute cancellation deadline; and the full native cross-platform reaper budget completes inside the 15-second web proxy budget.
Focused tests, local API/web verification, exact-head CI/review, rollout, public verification, and authenticated Hati balance proof pass.

constraints: Keep member authorization ahead of every private grocery response.
Keep Sheet, household, balance, token, nonce, and SSH material out of repository evidence.
Return retryable unavailability when the whole request budget is exhausted; pause automatic retry when native descendant cleanup is unconfirmed; never invent a zero balance.

evidence_refs: Production runtime events observed authenticated /api/grocery/totals responses at 24-31 seconds while the same-origin web proxy permits 15 seconds and the client permits 16 seconds.
The Hati page opened spend, sheet, shops, categories, and totals together; synchronous graph reads inside async handlers serialized those siblings on the event loop.
Abandoned totals requests continued after the proxy timeout and overlapped with client retries, amplifying the cold Sheet read instead of healing it.
After production pressure subsided, the existing second retry recovered the balance, proving Sheet availability and isolating scheduling/deadline composition as the failure.

Exact-head review found that canceling a to_thread awaiter alone leaves its database worker alive; membership and private-spend reads now carry the same absolute deadline into deadline_session, which cancels the active driver operation before the response invites retry.

Renewed exact-head review found that membership miss/error handling could start a separate ten-second Form policy call after the database deadline; the policy now receives only the remaining shared budget, reserves native child cleanup time, and is skipped as retryable after exhaustion.

A third exact-head review found the initial 0.25-second policy cleanup reserve was smaller than Windows taskkill plus communicate bounds; the membership lane now imports and reserves the native bridge's full two-step reaper budget, and a regression starts and reaps the policy before response.

A fourth exact-head review found the final balance policy still consumed the entire remaining request budget; one grocery policy-timeout helper now reserves the full native reaper budget for balance and reconciliation policies, with a started-policy endpoint regression.

A fifth exact-head review found the reaper's final communicate fallback was unbounded when descendants held pipes open; Form output now uses temporary files and every tree-termination wait is finite and included in the exported reserve.

A sixth exact-head review found that a direct Windows root kill did not prove the separately launched fkwu child had exited; the bounded reaper now retries tree-aware taskkill while ancestry is intact and fails closed when descendant termination cannot be confirmed.

A seventh exact-head review found generic policy handlers could erase the fail-closed cleanup signal and invite another request; a distinct cleanup exception now reaches HTTP 409 in membership, totals, and resync paths, which the Hati client treats as non-retryable.

An eighth exact-head review found two remaining erasure edges: final root-wait expiration now raises the same cleanup exception, and legacy reconciliation maps it to HTTP 409 outside the initial resync selection block.
No secret, token, nonce, household value, balance, private Sheet URL, or SSH material is present in this evidence.
